lines.text: Surprisingly, when Prince Darling was angry, his ring scemed to press harder
into his finger. But the ring did not prick him when his anger seemed far away.
Prince Darling did not think too much about this. He searched and searched for
animals for a long time but went home without any catch.
When Prince Darling arrived home
and went to his royal chambers, his little
dog Baby ran to meet him, jumping
round him with pleasure.
"Get away!" said Prince Darling, quite
angrily. "I don't want you. You are in the
way!"
The poor little dog, who didn't understand this at all, pulled Prince Darling's
coat to make him at least look at her, and this made the prince so cross that
he gave her a hard kick. Instantly his ring pricked him sharply, as though a pin
stuck in his finger. He was astonished, and sat down in a corner of his room,
feeling ashamed of himself.
"I believe the Fairy is laughing at me," he thought. "Surely I should not kick
a harmless animal!"
"I'm not making fun of you," said a voice, answering Prince Darling's
thoughts. "You have made two mistakes. First, you were angry because you
could not meet your hunting goal in the forest. Do you think that all men and
animals are only made to do your pleasure? Second, you were cruel to a poor
little animal who did not in the least deserve to be ill-treated. I know you are far
above a little dog, but if it were right that great people should ill-treat all who
are beneath them, I might at this moment beat you or kill you. A fairy is greater
than a man!"
